# Inklet: plotting guide for coding agents

Inklet makes publication figures in Python: plots sized in millimetres, text
measured so nothing overlaps, and SVG/PDF/PNG output that needs no hand fixing.
Use it like plotly express: one call per chart, columns named by string.

## One chart

```python
import inklet as i

chart = i.line(df, x='time', y='signal', color='condition')   # color= groups by a column
chart.save('signal.pdf', 'signal.png')                          # extension picks the format
```

`df` may be a pandas or Polars DataFrame, a dict of columns, a list of row
dicts, or a path to a CSV/TSV file (`i.line('results.csv', x=..., y=...)`).
Instead of a table, pass sequences: `i.line(x=[1, 2, 3], y=[2, 4, 3])`.

| Function | Columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `i.line(df, x, y, color=)` | `y` may be a list of columns; no `y` plots every numeric column; points are joined in x order (`sort=False` keeps row order) | `markers=True`, `error_y='col'` draws a band, `dash='dashed'`, `linewidth=` (mm); a missing y breaks the line there (`gaps='bridge'` joins across the gap instead); `secondary_y='col'` puts series on a right-hand axis (see below) |
| `i.scatter(df, x, y, color=, size=)` | numeric `color` column with many values gets a colour ramp and colour bar | `error_y='col'`, `text='col'` labels points clear of the marks (blank or missing labels are skipped); `secondary_y='group'` puts a colour group on the right |
| `i.bar(df, x, y, color=)` | `x` categories; rows with the same `x` are summed; no `y` counts rows | `agg='mean'` with `error_y='sem'`/`'sd'`/`'ci95'` and `points=True`; `stacked=True`, `orient='h'` |
| `i.hist(df, x, color=, bins=20)` | | `density=True`, `cumulative=True` |
| `i.kde(df, x, color=)` / `i.ecdf(df, x, color=)` | | `fill=True` on kde |
| `i.boxplot(df, x, y)` / `i.violin(df, x, y)` / `i.strip(df, x, y)` | `x` category column, `y` values | `points=True` overlays the samples |
| `i.area(df, x, y, color=)` | groups stack (values must be >= 0) | `stacked=False` overlays |
| `i.regression(df, x, y, color=)` | points + fitted line + confidence band | `method='linear'` or `'lowess'` |
| `i.heatmap(rows, x=col_labels, y=row_labels)` | or a long table: `i.heatmap(df, x=, y=, z=)` | first row is drawn at the top; `palette='viridis'` |
| `i.survival(df, time=, event=, color=)` | Kaplan-Meier curves, one per group; `event` is 1/True for an event, 0/False for censored | `at_risk=True` table, `pvalue=True` log-rank P for 2+ groups, `band='log-log'`; survival runs 0 to 1 |
| `i.volcano(df, x=, y=)` | `x` log2 fold change, `y` raw p-value | `label='col'` and `highlight=['name', ...]`, `q='col'` adjusted p colours by FDR |
| `i.quick.forest(df, label=, estimate=, lower=, upper=)` | one row per study with its interval | `weight='col'`, `summary='col'` for diamonds, `log=True`, `right=['ci', 'n']`; `i.forest(rows)` is the rows-list diagram |
| `i.pie(df, names=, values=)` | one slice per row, sized by `values`, labelled with shares | `hole=0.5` for a donut (a fraction of the radius); `legend='bottom'` or False, not a corner; `labels='value'` or a format |
| `i.lollipop(df, x=, y=)` | one dot per category on a stem from zero | `orient='h'` lays it across, rows top to bottom; `color=` is one colour; one row per category |
| `i.dumbbell(df, y=, x=['before', 'after'])` | two dots per category joined by a line; `y` the category, `x` the two value columns | the legend names the dots after the columns; rows top to bottom; a missing value draws no dot |
| `i.waterfall(df, x=, y=)` | changes as bars on a running total | `totals=['Start', 'End']` steps stand from zero; a missing change on a total shows the running total; `ylim=` overrides the fitted range |
| `i.slope(df, x=, y=, group=)` | each group's values at two or more time points, joined | `labels='both'` names the lines at their ends (no key); `format='{:.0f}%'`; `highlight=['name']` |

`color=` that is not a column name is a literal colour: `color='#c1121f'`.

PNG output is at the preset's resolution: 300 dpi for print presets, 150 for
slides. For more, pass `chart.save('fig.png', dpi=600)`. SVG and PDF are
vector and ignore `dpi`.

Chart options, accepted by every function above:

| Option | Values |
|---|---|
| `width` | `'single'` (89 mm, default), `'double'` (183 mm), `'slide'` (254 mm), or millimetres (`120`, `'120mm'`); unset, a Preset keeps its own page |
| `height` | millimetres; default is about 0.62 x width, 45-75 mm |
| `style` | preset name: `'scientific.modern'` (default: colour-led marks, grey axes), `'scientific.general'`, `'scientific.nature'`, `'scientific.science'`, `'scientific.cell'`, `'educational.textbook'`, `'marketing.report'`, `'marketing.presentation'`; or a Preset object, e.g. `i.preset('scientific.modern').customize(font_pt=12)` |
| `font_pt` | the main type size in points; ticks and the key take 6/7 of it and titles 9/7 |
| `palette` | `'okabe-ito'`, `'tol-bright'`, `'tol-muted'`, `'inklet'`, `'set2'`, `'dark2'`... or a list of colours |
| `title`, `xlabel`, `ylabel` | axis titles default to the column names |
| `xlim`, `ylim` | `(low, high)`; default fits the data. Explicit limits zoom: marks are cut at the axes |
| `xscale`, `yscale` | `'linear'` or `'log'` |
| `legend` | `'auto'` (default), `'direct'` (names at the line ends, no key), `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'left'`, `'right'`, a corner `'ne'`, or `False` |
| `facet_col`, `facet_row` | column names: one chart per value, on shared axes, in a grid; `facet_col_wrap=3` wraps |
| `facet_order` | the facet values in draw order: a list for every facet, or a dict of column name to list. Default: numbers and dates ascending, text in first-appearance order; a list must name every value |
| `grid` | `True`, `False`, `'x'`, `'y'` |
| `xticks`, `yticks` | the tick values to show, e.g. `xticks=[0, 5, 10, 15, 20]` |
| `xminor`, `yminor` | `True` for unlabelled minor ticks, or an integer: how many pieces each major step divides into |
| `xformat`, `yformat` | how tick numbers are written, as the axis `format=`: a `'{}'` spec such as `'{:.0%}'` or `'{:,.0f}'`, a suffix such as `'%'`, or a callable. Not for `forest` |

## Layering and annotating

Chart methods have the same names and arguments as the functions; each returns
the chart so calls chain:

```python
chart = i.scatter(df, x='dose', y='response', color='strain')
chart.line(fit, x='dose', y='predicted', color='#444444', name='model')
chart.hline(0.5, label='EC50')                     # any Panel method works on a chart
chart.annotate(3.0, 0.9, 'saturation')             # text placed clear of the data
chart.labels(x='Dose / mg kg^{-1}', y='Response', title='Dose response')
chart.save('dose.pdf')
```

Text markup: `**bold**`, `//italic//`, `x^{2}`, `H_{2}O`, `{#c1121f|coloured}`.

Two quantities in different units go on one chart with `secondary_y=`, a
column or a list of them (for `scatter`, colour groups):
`i.line(df, x='month', y=['rain', 'temp'], secondary_y='temp')`. That series
is drawn against a right-hand axis titled `temp`, in its colour when it is the
only series there, and the left axis fits only the rest. `labels(y2=)` retitles
the right axis. Two charts or small multiples are often clearer than two y
scales, so use it only when the quantities must share one x axis. A bar chart
with a line on the right is two calls: `i.bar(df, x, y='rain')`, then
`.line(df, x, y='temp', secondary_y='temp')` on the same chart.

`hline(y, label=)` and `vline(x, label=)` name a reference line at its end, and
the label is placed clear of the data: it is searched along the line and off
every mark on the panel, including marks drawn after the rule, so it does not
land on a bar. A labelled rule is drawn in front of the data (`front=True`
unless you say otherwise), because a line under a bar chart cannot be seen.
`label_side=` keeps the label to one side: `'n'` or `'s'` for an hline, `'e'`
or `'w'` for a vline.

## Small multiples

```python
i.line(df, x='time', y='signal', color='drug', facet_col='cell_line')          # one panel per cell line
i.scatter(df, x='dose', y='response', facet_row='replicate', facet_col='strain')
```

Facets share both axes, keep one colour per group across panels, show one key,
and drop repeated tick numbers and axis titles on inner panels.

## Multi-panel figures

`|` puts charts side by side, `/` stacks them. Panels get letters a, b, c...

```python
fig = (i.line(df, x='t', y='y') | i.boxplot(df, x='group', y='y')) / i.hist(df, x='y')
fig.save('figure1.pdf', 'figure1.png')
```

A row defaults to double-column width. Set the layout width with
`i.Layout('row', [a, b], width='double')` when building one explicitly.
If every chart in a row sets its width in millimetres, the row is as wide as
they are together, with the gaps between them, and each panel keeps its width:
`(i.line(df, x='t', y='y', width=60) | i.bar(df, x='g', y='v', width=120))` is
186 mm. A chart width the layout cannot use (a different page width on a
stacked layout, say) raises a `UserWarning`; set widths on the layout instead.

Figure options. `style`, `font_pt` and `grid` apply to the whole figure.
Set them on the layout, `i.Layout('row', [a, b], style='scientific.nature')`,
or after the fact with `fig.options(font_pt=8, grid=True)`, which returns the
layout. Left unset, the charts decide: charts that agree use their value, and
charts that disagree raise one `UserWarning` per setting, naming the values,
and the first chart's value is used. Palettes are per panel: each chart's own
`palette=` colours its own series, a palette set on the layout
(`fig.options(palette='okabe-ito')`) overrides them all, and a chart without
one takes the figure's (the first chart's). A series name keeps its palette
slot across the panels, so `'control'` is the same colour in every panel that
draws it, provided the panels share a palette.

## A figure for a slide

`width='slide'` makes a 254 mm page, and its labels are 14 pt by default, so the
figure reads from the back of a room without other changes:

```python
chart = i.line(df, x='time', y='signal', color='condition', width='slide')
chart.save('slide.png')
```

For a presentation's look, with larger titles and labels (20 pt), use
`style='marketing.presentation'`. To choose the size, pass `font_pt=`: the
labels are that many points, with ticks and the key at 6/7 of it, so
`font_pt=16` reads larger than the default on a slide. A slide page is 254 x 143 mm,
which fits a 16:9 slide, so put the image in at its own size.

## Check the result (do this every time)

1. `figure = chart.save('fig.png')` returns the compiled figure.
   `print(figure.report())` lists overlapping labels, clipped or tiny text, and
   data running outside the axes (`DATA_OUTSIDE`, with the range to set), a key
   drawn over data (`KEY_COVERS_DATA`, with the corners that are clear), and
   supplied ticks dropped for lack of room (`TICKS_DROPPED`), each with a
   suggested fix. `inklet lint: clean` means no problems. Mark ornamental text
   such as a pale watermark with `text(..., decorative=True)` so the contrast
   check skips it.
2. Look at the PNG. If you can view images, open it. Labels are measured, so
   overlaps are rare. Check that the right data are plotted, not just that it ran.
3. From a shell: `inklet check script.py --png preview.png` builds the script,
   prints the report, writes a preview, and exits 1 when there are errors
   (`--strict` also fails on warnings, `--json` gives machine-readable output).

A script that `check` or `build` loads supplies its figure one of two ways.
Define `make_document()`, `make_figure()` or `make_chart()` and return the
figure; the first one defined, in that order, is called. Or leave a Document,
Chart, Layout, CompiledFigure or Figure at module level. The figure is chosen
by type, so other module-level values (a matplotlib `fig`, a DataFrame) are
ignored. Name the figure `chart`, `doc`, `fig` or `figure` (first match wins)
when the script has several inklet objects. With no such name, the only inklet
object is used. Two unnamed ones are an error, and so is a script with none;
the error lists the module-level names it found.

`chart.show()` displays inline in Jupyter; outside a notebook it writes an SVG
and returns its path. Nothing opens a window or blocks, so scripts run headless.

## Units

Every length is millimetres: `width=120` is 120 mm. Font sizes are points
via `i.pt(8)`. Text is never shrunk to make things fit; if a figure is too
crowded, inklet reports it rather than drawing overlapping labels.

## Going further

A chart is a front end to the document model. When you need more control:

```python
spec = chart.spec               # the PlotSpec; any Panel method records on it
doc = chart.document()          # a Document with the chart in cell 'chart'
doc.add('diagram', i.box('Encoder'))   # add any other content
doc.compile().save('full.pdf')
```

The full model, which the quick API wraps:

```python
doc = i.preset('scientific.nature', format='double-column').document(columns=2)
plot = i.plot_spec()                       # axes fit the data; or x=(0, 10), y=(0, 1)
plot.line([(0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 2)], name='Signal')     # points are (x, y) rows
plot.scatter([(0, 1.2), (1, 2.8)], name='Samples')
plot.axes(x='Time / s', y='Signal / mV').legend()
doc.add('a', plot)
doc.add('b', other_plot, column=1, row=0)
doc.letters()
figure = doc.compile()
print(figure.report())
figure.save('figure.pdf')
```

`inklet guide --api` prints every plot method (more than 100: forest, volcano,
manhattan, survival curves, ridgelines, raincloud, sankey, upset, treemap,
networks, ternary...) with its signature.

- `i.from_matplotlib(fig)` redraws a matplotlib figure's data as Inklet charts,
  in Inklet's type and layout. What it does not carry (hatches, RGB images,
  figure-level text, twin axes, inset axes, and more) is listed in a
  `MatplotlibWarning`; `docs/matplotlib.md` has the full list.

## Common mistakes

- `i.box` is a diagram box, not a box plot. Use `i.boxplot`.
- Bars **sum** rows that share an `x` value. For a mean with an error bar use
  `i.bar(df, x='group', y='value', agg='mean', error_y='sem', points=True)`.
- `area` stacks; stacked values must be non-negative.
- `chart.twin_y(...)` is refused on a quick chart. For a second y scale use
  `secondary_y=`, as above.
- Do not call `plt.show()`-style display code; save files and inspect them.
- In the full model, `plot_spec(x=..., y=...)` does **not** clip: data past
  the domain are drawn outside the axes and reported as `DATA_OUTSIDE`. Leave
  `x`/`y` out to fit the data, or pass `clip=True`.

## Plot methods

Call these on a chart (`chart.volcano(...)`) or on `i.plot_spec()`.
Positional `points` are (x, y) rows; `groups` map a category to its samples.

- `annotate(x, y, text, *, side='n', clear=None, leader=True, inside=True, dot=False, front=True, **kwargs)`: A callout on one **data** point: a label clear of it, with a leader.
- `arc_diagram(nodes, edges, *, size=None, top=None, diameter=None, floor=None, shape='circle', shapes=None, groups=None, color=None, labels=True, rotate=None, weights=None, width=None, width_floor=None, edge_color=None, directed=False, opacity=0.8, label_size=None, **style)`: An arc diagram: nodes in a row, each edge a half-ellipse arc above them whose width is the edge weight.
- `arrow(a, b, *, head='triangle', label=None, front=True, **style)`: An arrow from one **data** point to another.
- `at_risk(*, ticks=None, count=5, title='Number at risk', font_size=None, pad=None, **kwargs)`: The number-at-risk table under the x axis of a `kaplan_meier` plot.
- `axes(x=None, y=None, *, x_options=None, y_options=None, **kwargs)`: Bottom and left axes with shared and per-axis options.
- `axis(side='bottom', *, at=None, **kwargs)`: Hang an axis off one edge, built from this panel's own scale.
- `background(**style)`: Fill the plot area, beneath everything already in it.
- `band(x, lo, hi, *, name=None, color=None, **style)`: The shaded envelope between two edges over shared x.
- `barplot(at, data, *, estimator='mean', error='sem', points=True, width=0.8, gap=0.12, orient='v', color=None, name=None, size=None, cap=None, baseline=0.0, **style)`: Bars of the mean with error bars and every observation as a dot.
- `bars(at, heights, *, width=0.8, baseline=0.0, orient='v', stacked=None, grouped=None, gap=0.12, color=None, bar_colors=None, name=None, labels=None, label_position='auto', label_options=None, normalize=False, **style)`: A rectangle per value, standing on a baseline.
- `bland_altman(a, b, *, z=1.96, percent=False, confidence=None, labels=True, format='{:.2f}', color=None, size=None, name=None, **style)`: A Bland-Altman (mean-difference) plot of two methods' agreement.
- `boxen(groups, *, at=None, width=0.8, orient='v', depth='tukey', outliers=True, color=None, size=None, **style)`: Letter-value (boxen) plots: nested boxes out into the tails.
- `boxplot(groups, *, at=None, width=0.6, orient='v', whisker=1.5, outliers=True, color=None, **style)`: Quartile boxes with Tukey whiskers, one per group.
- `bracket(x0, x1, y=None, **kwargs)`: A grouping or significance bracket across a data span.
- `brackets(comparisons, *, format='stars', hide_ns=False, stars=None, ns='ns', **kwargs)`: Significance brackets for many pairs of groups, stacked clear of each other.
- `break_marks()`: Draw the break glyph wherever a `inklet.broken` scale interrupts.
- `bullet(at, values, *, targets=None, ranges=None, baseline=0.0, orient='h', width=0.7, color=None, **style)`: Bullet charts: a measure bar against a target and qualitative ranges.
- `bump(values, *, at=None, ranked=False, labels='both', color=None, highlight=None, size=None, numbers=False, **style)`: A bump chart: the rank of each series at each time point.
- `calendar(values, *, start=None, end=None, ramp=None, scale=None, center=None, week_start='monday', gap=0.25, labels=True, **style)`: A calendar heatmap: a square per day, a column per week.
- `chord(matrix, name=None, *, color=None, gap=2.0, start=-90.0, directed=False, sort=False, thickness=None, pad=None, labels=True, opacity=0.72, color_by='source', size=None, **style)`: A chord diagram: groups as arcs around a ring, flows between them as ribbons through the middle, fitted into the plot area.
- `clusters(groups, *, color=None, highlight=None, highlight_color=None, width=None, labels=False, size=None, min_size=1, **style)`: Boxes on the diagonal of a matrix, one per cluster.
- `colorbar(*, side='right', source=None, corner=None, scale=None, length=None, pad=None, plate=False, title=None, **kwargs)`: The ramp this panel's matrix was coloured through, as a key beside it.
- `correlogram(r, name=None, *, triangle='lower', shape='circle', ramp=None, values=False, labels=True, size=None, **style)`: A correlation matrix as a triangle of glyphs sized and coloured by r.
- `dendrogram(tree, *, labels=None, orient='v', threshold=None, color=None, **style)`: The merge tree of a hierarchical clustering, drawn as elbows.
- `density_scatter(points, *, bandwidth=None, ramp=None, size=None, sort=True, raster=False, dpi=300, marker='circle', **style)`: A scatter coloured by how crowded each point's neighbourhood is.
- `diverging_bars(at, left, right, *, orient='h', width=0.7, color=None, name=None, reference=None, titles=None, zero=True, **style)`: Two quantities per category, back to back: left of zero and right.
- `dotplot(sizes=None, colors=None, *, x=None, y=None, top=None, diameter=None, ramp=None, scale=None, center=None, color=None, size=None, **style)`: A dot plot: a circle per cell, its area one value, its colour another.
- `dumbbell(at, values, *, orient='v', size=None, color=None, name=None, marker='circle', connector=None, **style)`: Two or more dots per category joined by a line: a dumbbell plot.
- `ecdf(values, *, weights=None, complementary=False, normalize=True, extend=True, name=None, **style)`: The empirical cumulative distribution of `values` as a step line.
- `embedding(points, clusters, *, color=None, size=None, labels=True, center='median', label_size=None, arrows=None, shuffle=True, seed=0, raster=False, outline=None, outline_core=0.8, **style)`: A UMAP or t-SNE style scatter, coloured and named by cluster.
- `errorbars(points, *, yerr=None, xerr=None, cap=None, **style)`: Whiskers through each point, in the data's own units.
- `fill(points, *, baseline=0.0, orient='v', name=None, **style)`: The area between a series and a baseline.
- `fill_between(x, y0, y1, *, name=None, **style)`: The band between two curves over shared x -- a confidence envelope.
- `gantt(tasks, *, groups=None, color=None, width=0.6, labels=False, **style)`: A Gantt chart: a bar per task from its start to its end.
- `grid(*, x=True, y=True, count=5, x_options=None, y_options=None, **style)`: Rules at the tick positions, under the data.
- `guide(a, b, *, label=None, at=0.5, offset=1.0, label_style=None, **style)`: A straight data guide with a label following its displayed direction.
- `hexbin(points, *, gridsize=24, min_count=1, ramp=None, scale=None, log=False, **style)`: Points counted in hexagons, each coloured by its count.
- `hist(values, bins=10, *, range=None, density=False, baseline=0.0, orient='v', color=None, name=None, histtype=None, cumulative=False, **style)`: Binned counts as touching rectangles.
- `hist2d(points, bins=20, *, range=None, density=False, min_count=1, ramp=None, scale=None, log=False, **style)`: A 2D histogram: points counted in rectangular bins on continuous axes, each bin coloured by its count.
- `hline(y, *, span=None, front=None, label=None, label_side=None, **style)`: A horizontal rule at one **data** value of y.
- `hspan(y0, y1, *, front=False, **style)`: A shaded stripe between two **data** values of y, full width.
- `icicle(data, *, orient='h', root=None, gap=None, spacing=None, links=None, color=None, highlight=None, highlight_color=None, labels='fit', levels=False, counts=False, sort=False, size=None, **style)`: An icicle (partition) chart: one band per level of a hierarchy, each node spanning its share of its parent.
- `inset(sub, **kwargs)`: Put a smaller panel in a corner of this one. See `plot.inset`.
- `kaplan_meier(data, *, confidence=0.95, band='log-log', shade=True, censors=True, color=None, pvalue=None, pvalue_corner='sw', **style)`: Kaplan-Meier survival curves, with censor ticks and confidence bands.
- `kde(values, *, bandwidth='scott', adjust=1.0, cut=3.0, samples=200, fill=False, stat='density', orient='v', color=None, name=None, baseline=0.0, **style)`: A kernel density curve, or one per group.
- `kde2d(points, *, levels=5, fill=False, bandwidth='scott', adjust=1.0, gridsize=96, color=None, ramp=None, name=None, **style)`: Contours of a 2D kernel density: lines, or filled levels.
- `label_lines(name=None, **kwargs)`: Name curves at the curves themselves instead of in a legend.
- `label_points(points, labels, **kwargs)`: Label many data points at once, clear of the marks and each other.
- `legend(*, corner='ne', side=None, entries=None, columns=None, max_width=None, swatch=None, pad=None, plate=None, title=None, markup=True, order='row', col_gap=None, row_gap=None, names=None, **style)`: A key built from the series this panel actually drew.
- `likert(at, counts, *, neutral=None, normalize=True, orient='h', width=0.7, color=None, name=None, labels=None, zero=True, **style)`: Diverging stacked bars for Likert-scale responses, centred on neutral.
- `line(points, *, smooth=0.0, closed=False, name=None, err=None, err_style='band', simplify=None, **style)`: A path through data points: straight by default, curved with `smooth`.
- `lollipop(at, values, *, baseline=0.0, orient='v', size=None, color=None, marker='circle', stem=None, name=None, **style)`: One value per category as a dot on a stem from `baseline`.
- `ma(mean, fold, p=None, *, labels=None, top=10, fold_threshold=1.0, p_threshold=0.05, color=None, name=None, size=None, log=True, zero=True, **style)`: An MA plot: mean expression on x against log2 fold change on y.
- `map(points)`: `point()` over a sequence: data pairs in, millimetres out.
- `matrix(values, *, ramp=None, scale=None, center=None, x=None, y=None, overlap=None, missing=None, vector='cells', interpolation='nearest', samples=4, raster='auto', **style)`: A 2D array of values, one coloured cell each.
- `mosaic(at, values, *, color=None, name=None, gap=0.6, labels=None, categories=True, **style)`: A mosaic (Marimekko) chart: stacked bars as wide as their totals.
- `network(nodes, edges, *, layout='circular', order=None, size=None, top=None, diameter=None, floor=None, shape='circle', shapes=None, groups=None, color=None, labels='auto', label_size=None, weights=None, width=None, width_floor=None, edge_color=None, bend=None, arrows=False, opacity=0.85, gap=None, iterations=300, **style)`: A weighted network: node area from a value, edge width from a weight, colours from categories, fitted into the plot area.
- `outline(**style)`: A rectangle around the area, drawn over the data.
- `parallel(rows, *, dimensions=None, ranges=None, color=None, groups=None, count=4, format=None, labels=True, **style)`: Parallel coordinates: an axis per variable and a line per record.
- `pp(values, *, dist='normal', color=None, size=None, name=None, **style)`: A probability-probability plot against a fitted normal.
- `pyramid(at, left, right, *, titles=None, color=None, width=0.92, **kwargs)`: A population pyramid: `diverging_bars` with touching bars.
- `qq(values, *, dist='normal', line='quartiles', color=None, size=None, name=None, **style)`: A normal quantile-quantile plot: sample against theoretical quantiles, with a reference line.
- `raincloud(groups, *, at=None, orient='h', width=0.9, bandwidth=None, samples=64, cut=2.0, whisker=1.5, points='jitter', size=None, seed=0, box=True, color=None, **style)`: A half violin, a narrow box and the observations, per group.
- `rect(x0, y0, x1, y1, *, front=False, **style)`: A rectangle whose four sides are **data** values -- a gated region, the extent of an inset, a box round a cluster.
- `region(x0, y0, x1, y1)`: Map two data corners to a normalized rectangle in panel coordinates.
- `regression(points, *, method='linear', confidence=0.95, prediction=False, scatter=True, frac=0.6666666666666666, iterations=3, span=None, color=None, size=None, name=None, **style)`: Points with a fitted line and its confidence band.
- `residuals(points, *, method='linear', frac=0.6666666666666666, iterations=3, smooth=False, color=None, size=None, name=None, **style)`: The residuals of a fit against x, with a zero line.
- `ribbon(a, b, **kwargs)`: A Sankey band from data point `a` to data point `b`.
- `ridgeline(groups, *, at=None, overlap=1.5, bandwidth=None, samples=96, scale='shared', fit=True, color=None, **style)`: Overlapping kernel densities, one per category: a ridgeline plot.
- `scatter(points, *, size=None, color=None, ramp=None, scale=None, marker='circle', name=None, hollow=False, raster=False, dpi=300, **style)`: Markers at data points, with size and colour that may be data too.
- `sina(groups, *, at=None, width=0.8, orient='v', bandwidth='scott', adjust=1.0, size=None, seed=0, color=None, marker='circle', **style)`: A sina plot: points jittered within their group's density.
- `size_key(source=None, *, side='right', corner=None, values=None, count=3, format=None, title=None, orient=None, pad=None, plate=False, **style)`: Reference circles with their values: the key to a size encoding.
- `slope(values, *, at=None, labels='both', format=None, color=None, highlight=None, size=None, name=True, **style)`: A slope chart: each series' values at a few time points, joined.
- `split_violin(first, second, *, at=None, orient='v', width=0.8, bandwidth=None, samples=64, cut=2.0, scale='shared', median=True, quartiles=False, color=None, name=None, **style)`: Two conditions per category as the two halves of one violin.
- `stackarea(x, values, *, baseline=0.0, color=None, name=None, **style)`: Stack non-negative series over shared x values, in supplied order.
- `stem(points, *, baseline=0.0, orient='v', color=None, marker='circle', size=None, hollow=False, rule=True, name=None, **style)`: A stem plot: a stem from `baseline` to a dot at each `(x, y)`.
- `step(points, *, where='post', name=None, **style)`: A staircase through the points, for a quantity that changes at instants rather than continuously.
- `streamgraph(x, values, *, offset='wiggle', order='input', color=None, name=None, smooth=0.5, **style)`: A streamgraph: stacked areas around a moving baseline.
- `strip(groups, *, at=None, width=0.8, jitter=0.5, orient='v', size=None, seed=0, color=None, marker='circle', **style)`: A strip plot: each group's observations, jittered across its slot.
- `sunburst(data, *, inner=0.3, start=-90.0, color=None, highlight=None, highlight_color=None, labels=True, center=None, sort=False, size=None, **style)`: A sunburst: an icicle chart bent into rings about the centre of the plot area, the first level innermost.
- `swarm(groups, *, at=None, width=0.8, max_width=None, orient='v', size=None, gap=None, marker='circle', hollow=False, color=None, **style)`: Every observation as its own dot, nudged sideways until none hides another.
- `ternary(points, *, labels=None, ticks=5, grid=True, total=100, format=None, color=None, size=None, marker='circle', name=None, **style)`: Compositions of three parts as points in a triangle.
- `text(x, y, content, *, anchor='center', offset=(0.0, 0.0), size=None, markup=True, front=True, decorative=False, **style)`: Words at one **data** point.
- `timeline(events, *, at=None, color=None, size=None, levels=None, line=True, **style)`: An event timeline: labelled stems off a base line.
- `title(content, *, align='center', pad=None)`: A heading over the panel, clear of whatever is already in it.
- `treemap(data, *, color=None, highlight=None, highlight_color=None, padding=None, header=None, labels=True, values=None, sort=True, size=None, **style)`: A squarified treemap: each leaf a rectangle with area proportional to its value, filling the plot area.
- `twin_x(scale=None, *, side='top', label=None, color=None, axis=True, **kwargs)`: A second x scale over the same area -- wavelength above frequency, or a second time base. `twin_y` explains the shape of it.
- `twin_y(scale=None, *, side='right', label=None, color=None, axis=True, **kwargs)`: A second y scale over the same area, and a handle that draws in it.
- `violin(groups, *, at=None, width=0.8, orient='v', bandwidth=None, samples=64, cut=2.0, median=True, color=None, **style)`: Mirrored kernel densities, one per group.
- `vline(x, *, span=None, front=None, label=None, label_side=None, **style)`: A vertical rule at one **data** value of x -- stimulus onset, a dose, a cut point. `span=(y0, y1)` clips it in data coordinates.
- `volcano(fold, p, *, labels=None, top=None, fold_threshold=1.0, p_threshold=0.05, color=None, name=None, size=None, thresholds=True, label_options=None, highlight=None, q=None, **style)`: A volcano plot: log2 fold change on x against -log10 p on y.
- `vspan(x0, x1, *, front=False, **style)`: A shaded stripe between two **data** values of x, full height.
- `waffle(values, *, rows=10, columns=10, total=None, color=None, name=None, gap=0.18, order='column', **style)`: A waffle chart: shares of a whole as cells of a grid.
- `waterfall(at, values, *, totals=(), baseline=0.0, orient='v', width=0.6, color=None, connectors=True, labels=None, name=None, **style)`: A waterfall chart: signed changes as bars floating on a running total.
- `width_key(source=None, *, side='right', corner=None, values=None, count=3, format=None, title=None, color=None, length=None, pad=None, plate=False)`: Reference lines with their weights: the key to an edge-width encoding.
